name: Niagara–Buffalo hydroelectric supply
summary: In November 1896 Westinghouse alternating-current equipment began sending hydroelectric power from Niagara Falls to a Buffalo railway company under contract.
description: Westinghouse alternating-current dynamos and transmission of hydroelectric power from Niagara Falls to Buffalo.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Niagara Falls offered enormous water power, and the nearby city of Buffalo was a large market that could be reached by transmission line.

market.note: The contemporary account records a contract for 1,000 horsepower and actual delivery to the Buffalo Railway Company. This does not establish the first sale or general tariff.

evidence.locator: Electrical Review 18 November 1896, pp. 247–249, headline and first paragraphs
evidence.supports: Hydroelectric power was delivered under contract from Niagara Falls to the Buffalo Railway Company just after midnight on 16 November 1896.

links.statement: The Electricity Council chronology says the 1891 Frankfurt transmission gave impetus to the Niagara Falls two-phase scheme, which later supplied Buffalo.
links.scope: Influence on the general Niagara scheme and long-distance AC power, not identical equipment or phase count.
links.alternatives: Ames, the Chicago exposition, Tesla and Westinghouse polyphase work and other projects supplied alternative or additional influences.
links.caveats: The chronology is an OCR text copy and the exact decision pathway is not shown; the Niagara generating scheme and Buffalo transmission had different phase arrangements.
links.timing: 1891 exhibition precedes Niagara project decisions and the documented 1896 service.
